title: Home Alone
logline: A boy is accidentally left at home when his family flies to Paris for Christmas, and two burglars pick the wrong house.
why: The plot is carried by places and objects, so a missed line never means a lost scene. Family vocabulary, daily routines and short, concrete dialogue repeat often enough to stick.
language: American English, mostly simple sentences; the burglars talk fast in a few scenes, and Kevin's older brother mumbles on purpose.
content: Slapstick violence and cartoon traps; nobody is seriously hurt. Suitable for all ages.

scenes.title: The head count
scenes.task: Count the family members who run through the airport. Who is missing, and who finally notices?

scenes.title: Dinner for one
scenes.task: Pause on Kevin's plate. Name everything he eats, then compare it with your own ideal dinner.

scenes.title: The burglars' plan
scenes.task: The burglars name the houses they will rob and when. Predict: what will Kevin do about it?

scenes.title: Welcome to the traps
scenes.task: List three traps in the order they happen. Which one made the room laugh loudest?

words.def: a person who breaks into a house to steal
words.ex: The burglars watch the house from a van.

words.def: the room under the roof of a house
words.ex: Kevin hides in the attic when he is scared.

words.def: a person who lives next to you
words.ex: The old neighbour is not as scary as he looks.

words.def: a thing that catches or hurts someone
to make a loud, high sound when afraid
words.ex: Marv screams when the spider lands on him.
At first, Kevin loves being alone.

questions: Why does Kevin's family fly to Paris without him? Whose fault is it, really?
What is the first thing Kevin does when he understands that he is alone? What would you do?
Kevin says he wants his family to disappear — and then they do. Is the film a wish come true or a lesson?
Which trap is the cleverest, and which one is just cruel?
Why is Kevin afraid of the old man next door, and what changes his mind?
In your country, at what age can a child stay home alone? Is Kevin old enough?
Is Kevin a good boy or a difficult boy? Give two examples from the film.
Which line from the film would you repeat to a friend as a joke? Try to say it the same way.

gaps.line: When I grow up and get married, I'm living ___!
This is my house. I have to ___ it.

quotes.quote: Kevin! What did you do to my room?
quotes.note: Buzz is the older brother — and the reason Kevin gets sent to the attic.

quotes.quote: Keep the change, you filthy animal.
quotes.note: Kevin learns it from a black-and-white gangster film and uses it as his own line.
He says it as a joke — and then starts to believe it.

quiz.q: Where does the family fly for Christmas?
quiz.why: They fly to Paris and leave Kevin behind in Chicago.

quiz.q: Who does Kevin meet in the church?
quiz.why: The old man whose son he is afraid of — the meeting changes how Kevin sees him.

quiz.q: What time do the burglars plan to enter the house?
quiz.why: They say they will come at nine, so Kevin prepares the house before that.

quiz.q: How does Kevin finally get help?
quiz.why: The old neighbour arrives with a snow shovel — and the burglars run into the police.

quiz.q: Why is Kevin sad at the end?
options: He understands that being alone is not fun
He must go back to school
quiz.why: He wanted his family gone, then discovered that he wanted them back.

roleplay.title: The head count
roleplay.setting: Airport check-in at 7 a.m. The family is late, the queue is long, and nobody is counting children.

roles.brief: You are the mother. You are stressed, you have five children, a passport for each one and no time for jokes. Keep asking the clerk to hurry.
You work for the airline. You have heard every excuse. You are polite but very slow, and you keep finding problems with the documents.
You are eight. You are in the middle of this chaos. You are asked nothing and say almost nothing — until the one moment it matters.

roleplay.challenge: Play the scene twice: once as a comedy, once as a disaster film. Then swap roles and see who notices the missing child.

quest.title: Station 1 · The missing passenger
quest.task: At the airport the family counts heads. How many people are travelling, and how many do they count? Find the moment and write both numbers.

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt
quest.task: Find in the film: a word for the room under the roof, a word for a person who steals from houses, and a word for a person living next door.

quest.title: Station 3 · Trap designers
quest.task: Invent one new trap for the burglars using only things you can see in a classroom. Describe it in three sentences, then act it out in slow motion.
quest.answer: Any plausible three-sentence design, acted out

quest.title: Station 4 · The order of things
quest.task: Put these four events in order: the pizza delivery, the fake party, the tarantula on Marv's face, the old neighbour's snow shovel.
quest.answer: pizza, fake party, tarantula, snow shovel
